newsitem.title: UK: LME chairman welcomes UK regulatory reforms.
newsitem.headline: LME chairman welcomes UK regulatory reforms.

text.p: Chairman of the London Metal Exchange (LME) Raj Bagri welcomed the planned reform of Britain's Financial Services Act announced on Tuesday.
Chancellor Gordon Brown unveiled plans to transfer responsibility for supervising banks from the Bank of England to a strengthened Securities and Investment Board.

"Although the statement does not directly affect the recognised investment exchanges (RIEs) such as the LME, the integrated approach announced by the chancellor will undoubtedly benefit investors, industry and other users of the LME alike," Bagri said in a statement.
"We hope that when detailed legislation is drafted, issues of vital importance to the smooth and effective functioning of the RIEs will also be properly addressed," he added.
LME Chief Executive David King, in Spain for a copper conference, said his first reaction to Brown's plans were that they were "bold and positive for the market".
